messages:
maya: FYI the mkdocs rollout created a few weird fragments. CI linkcheck flags percent-encoded anchors and duplicated redirect entries.

alex: can you share an example? i want to triage whether this is a build-time slugify mismatch or stale redirect metadata.

maya: sure. found in docs/guides/infra.md — heading is `## Getting started 🚀` but links are resolving to `/guides/#%F0%9F%9A%80-getting-started` on staging and 404.

kevin: that looks like URL-encoding of emoji in the fragment. older slugifier produced `🚀-getting-started` whereas the new one drops emoji and yields `getting-started`. nginx sees both in the redirect map and throws on duplicates.

sophia: short-term we can replace inbound links to the ascii anchor. long-term we should ensure the redirect map generator normalizes fragments to the canonical slug only.

maya: i ran a grep and found ~27 headings across the repo that include emoji or ZWJ sequences. quick list:

maya: ```
$ rg "^## .*[\u{1F300}-\u{1F6FF}]" docs/ -n
docs/guides/infra.md:14:## Getting started 🚀
docs/tutorials/setup.md:8:## Quick setup ⚡
... (trimmed)
```

alex: can we script a backfill that appends explicit IDs for those headings? like `## Getting started {#getting-started}` — then links won't break even if slugifier changes.

kevin: i can add a tiny mkdocs plugin that canonicalizes anchors to ascii-only slugs during build and emits a `data-slug` attribute so the linkcheck knows the canonical. that avoids editing content. plugin PR would include unit tests.

sophia: sounds good. for stability i'd prefer both: plugin + a one-off content backfill for critical pages. also add a note to the migration doc warning authors about emoji in headings.

mkdocs-bot: BUILD: linkcheck failed — 1 broken fragment -> /guides/#%F0%9F%9A%80-getting-started

maya: i'll take the manual backfill for guides and tutorials i maintain. will open a PR with explicit ids and update any local links.

kevin: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/901 — mkdocs plugin to normalize slug generation + tests.

alex: nice. i'll land maya's backfill PR first (hotfix path), run linkcheck on staging, then merge the plugin PR and do a full linkcheck run. can someone add a linter rule to warn on emoji in headings?

sophia: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/241 — add docs-linter rule and migration note. i'll also update the redirect map generator with `--dedupe-fragments`.

maya: PR 899 (backfill) opened, CI green for the subset. leaving this thread open until plugin + redirect dedupe land and the site rebuilds clean.

alex: thanks — please ping once staging passes. :handshake:
